extracted.intended_audience: medical researchers, journal editors, press officers, and health/medical journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical criteria for identifying and measuring 'spin' (misrepresentation) in press releases and related news coverage of randomized controlled trials, and for assessing whether press releases/news lead to misinterpretation of trial results compared with full articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'spin'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Spin" defined as specific reporting (intentional or unintentional) that emphasizes the beneficial effect of the experimental treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the central outcome of the study; classification of "spin" adapted from previous work. Examples include focusing on statistically significant results, interpreting nonsignificant primary outcomes as equivalence, inappropriate extrapolation, or inadequate claims of safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spin: focus on statistically significant results
rubrics_metrics.description: A focus on statistically significant results (within-group comparison, secondary outcomes, subgroup analyses, modified population of analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as a distinct type of spin; overemphasis on secondary/significant subgroup findings rather than primary outcome results can mislead interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spin: interpreting nonsignificant primary outcomes as equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: An interpretation of statistically nonsignificant results for the primary outcomes as showing treatment equivalence or comparable effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes statements treating p>0.05 as demonstrating equivalence; explicitly flagged as inappropriate in abstracts, press releases, and news items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spin: inadequate claim of safety or emphasis of benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Any inadequate claim of safety or emphasis of the beneficial effect of the treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include overstating safety without adequate data or emphasizing benefits beyond what primary outcomes support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spin: inappropriate extrapolation / no acknowledgement of nonsignificant primary outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Inappropriate extrapolation of results or failure to acknowledge nonstatistically significant primary outcomes in conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples observed: no acknowledgement of nonsignificant primary outcomes, or drawing broader causal/clinical claims than data warrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release should provide basic information for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release should provide journalists with the basic information needed to develop a news story and publish it in the mass media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press releases are meant to summarize key findings, contextualize them for journalists, and provide contact details/quotes; by being condensed they lack details but should avoid spin and provide caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide easy access to the research article
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide easy access to the research article (i.e., a direct link or the full reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered a quality marker; in the sample half of press releases provided easy access. Including the link/reference helps journalists verify findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report funding source
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the funding source of the study in the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about funding is a press-release quality criterion; only 36% of press releases in the sample reported funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report primary outcomes with numerical results rather than words only
rubrics_metrics.description: Report results for primary outcomes with numbers (not only words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the sample, results for primary outcomes were reported with words only in 41% of press releases; numeric reporting improves precision and reduces misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention and quantify safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention safety and, where possible, quantify adverse events in the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety was mentioned in 34% and quantified in 20% of press releases; inadequate or absent safety information contributes to misleading emphasis on benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report study limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the study's limitations in the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 14% of press releases reported limitations in this sample; including limitations is an important quality criterion to avoid overinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include quotations and characterize tone (emphasis vs moderation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quotations from authors or editors; quotations may report results with emphasis (e.g., "this work paves the way") or with moderation (e.g., "further investigation is needed").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 58 press releases (83%) contained quotations; the tone of quotes can amplify spin or provide appropriate caution—monitor for emphasis phrases versus moderating language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment/interpretation scale (1–5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation scale: 1 = definitely get the experimental treatment; 2 = probably get; 3 = decide for themselves (neutral); 4 = probably not get; 5 = definitely not get.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For analysis, scores 1–2 = treatment considered beneficial; 3 = neutral; 4–5 = not beneficial. Used to compare interpretations from article, press release, and news item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of misinterpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Misinterpretation defined as interpretation of the press release or news items differing from that based on the full-text article by at least one class according to the three-class system (beneficial / neutral / not beneficial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misinterpretation can be an overestimation or underestimation of treatment effect (e.g., press release rated beneficial while article rated neutral).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data abstraction standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a standardized data-abstraction form; preliminarily test the form; use two independent reviewers for subjective items with discrepancies resolved by consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study tested the form, reported mean kappa for "spin" assessments (0.56), and used dual-review for subjective determinations to improve reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding assessors when evaluating press releases/news items
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing press releases, assessors should be blinded to the authors of the press release, content of the scientific article, and journal of publication; for news items, assessors should be blinded to the press release and article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blinding was used in the study to reduce bias in evaluating how sources might lead to misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for press releases (for analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include press releases for published two-arm, parallel-group RCTs; exclude equivalence/noninferiority, cross-over, cluster, multiple-arm trials, follow-up studies, non-English releases, releases about more than one study, and duplicates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to create a homogeneous sample for study of spin in RCT press releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variables to consider when evaluating associations with spin
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider journal type (specialized vs general), funding source, sample size, type of treatment (drug vs other), results of primary outcomes (all nonstatistically significant vs other), author of the press release, and presence of spin in the article abstract conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the study, the main factor associated with spin in press releases was spin in the article abstract conclusions (RR 5.6). These variables are candidate predictors of press-release/news spin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical-analysis standards for associational evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use bivariate tests (chi-square, Fisher exact, Student t-test) and multivariable modelling (Poisson regression with robust error variance) with bootstrap model selection (1,000 samples); include variables with p<0.25 in bivariate analysis for possible inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an analytic framework for identifying factors associated with spin and misinterpretation while avoiding overfitting in multivariable models.
